3.  Fiscal Year 2025-2026 Third Quarter Treasurer’s Report
  State and Municipal Codes require the Treasurer to submit within
  30 days following each fiscal quarter a report summarizing the City’s cash and
  investment balances.
  Recommended Action
  Adopt the resolution accepting the FY25-26 Third Quarter Treasurer’s Report.

4.  Waterside Project Change Conditions of Use— Catalina Snorkel and Scuba
  The applicant has submitted a Waterside Project Application to amend conditions of use
  of their current waterside permit. Currently, the waterside permit authorizes
  snorkeling/dive tours and instruction emanating from Lover’s Cove and Casino Point.
  Applicant is requesting to add the services of unfouling propellers and light salvage within
  City waters.
  Recommended Action
  Make the affirmative finding that conditions set forth in the Avalon Municipal Code have
  been met and grant the amendment to the current Waterside Permit to Catalina Snorkel
  and Scuba and add additional services, with the following: 1. Catalina Snorkel and Scuba
  will add the service of unwrapping fouled propellers and general light salvage and retrieval
  of items lost overboard within the Harbor. 2. All personnel conducting dive services will
  have the appropriate dive certifications and training. 3. When conducting any dive
  operations Catalina Snorkel and Scuba will notify and obtain permission from the Harbor
  Department prior to the dive. 4. When diving in the Harbor, Catalina Scuba and Snorkel
  personnel will display a highly visible dive flag and take all precautions to avoid any boat
  traffic.5. If a skiff or boat is to be used in providing these services, all required and current
  registration/documentation will be provided to the Harbor Department.

PUBLIC HEARING

5.  Public Hearing to Receive Comment on the City’s FY 26-27 Community Development
  Block Grant (CDBG Funds
  The City of Avalon participates in the Los Angeles County Community Development’s
  Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Program. Per the terms of the CDBG
 CITY COUNCIL AGENDA

  Program, the City provided a 30-day public notice for members of the public to submit
  public comment in advance of a public hearing to review the City’s transfer of funds into
  the program’s Revolving Grant Fund.
  Recommended Action
  1. Open the duly noticed Public Hearing and receive comment. 2. Close the Public
  Hearing. 3. Approve the City’s estimated FY 26-27 Community Development Block Grant
  (CDBG) Funds to transfer into the Revolving Grant Fund. 4. Adopt a resolution authorizing
  the allocation of CDBG Funds for Fiscal Year 26-27.

GENERAL BUSINESS

6.  Professional Services Agreement for On-Call Planning Consultant
  In February 2024, City Council authorized a professional services agreement with
  Sagecrest Planning and Environmental, LLC (‘Sagecrest”) for on-call planning consultant
  services for a not-to-exceed contract sum of $150,000. An influx of planning activity,
  coupled with the large-scale development projects, has generated significant increased
  activity in the department not seen in recent years.
  Recommended Action
  1. Authorize an amendment to the current fiscal year professional services agreement
  with Sagecrest Planning and Environmental, LLC for a not-to-exceed sum of $225,000.
  2. Authorize the City Manager or designee to execute a budget adjustment transferring
  $50,000 from the General Planning/LCP Update Account Fund (10255-6781) to the
  Planning Professional Services Account (10255-5005). 3. Authorize a budget amendment
  in the amount of $25,000 to the Planning Professional Services Account (10255-5005).
  4. Authorize the City Manager to negotiate and execute a professional services
  agreement with Sagecrest Planning and Environmental, LLC for on-call planning
  consultant services for a two-year term for an annual cumulative total not to exceed
  amount of $200,000.00 commencing in FY 26-27.

7.  On-Call Consulting Services Contract Amendment for International Consulting Services,
  Inc.
  In May 2025, the City Council authorized an agreement with International Consulting
  Services, Inc. (ICS) for a three-year term, and a not-to-exceed contract sum of $100,000
  annually. ICS provides specialized construction and project management services on
  certain capital improvement projects. ICS is currently engaged with City Staff on a number
  of complex CIP projects, including Workforce Housing and Cabrillo Mole Rehabilitation
  Projects.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize the City Manager to negotiate and execute the second amendment to the
  Professional Services Agreement with International Consulting Services, Inc. for a not-to
  exceed additional sum of $140,000 total of $240,000— for the 12-month period of May
  —

  7, 2026 to May 6, 2027.

8.  ENGEO On-Call Engineering Services Contract
  ENGEO, Inc. has been used to provide geotechnical engineering resources including
  development of the geotechnical investigation of the Cabrillo Mole Multimodal
  Transportation Hub in September 2021, Geotechnical Exploration reports for 206 E.
  Whittley Ave., South Beach Seawall and Beach Restoration Plans, the Green Pleasure
  Pier and Club Dock Pile Installation Projects and many others City Capital Improvement
  Plan Projects.
  Recommended Action
  1. Make the affirmative finding that the City will not gain a competitive advantage by
  bidding and can contract work more economically or efficiently pursuant to Avalon
  Municipal Code Section 3-4.111(c), and 2. Award a professional services contract for on-
  call engineering, materials testing and inspection for an amount not-to-exceed an annual
  cumulative total for all services of $100,000 to ENGEO, Inc. for a three-year term.

9.  Cabrillo Mole Geotechnical Study Drilling RFP and Contract Award
  In order to begin the Cabrillo Mole Revitalization Project, the City must provide the
  selected Cabrillo Mole Revitalization Project contractor an updated geotechnical study
  that reflects current building code standards as well as the current geotechnical conditions
  of the substructure of the Cabrillo Mole. In order for any geotechnical engineer to perform
  an analysis, exploration pits must be drilled from the Cabrillo Mole’s surface.
  Recommended Action
  1. Authorize City Staff to develop and solicit a request for proposals for qualified firms to
  conduct drilling services to accommodate a geotechnical study to support the Cabrillo
  Mole Revitalization Project. 2. Pursuant to Avalon Municipal Code Section 3-4.205,
  authorize the City Manager to negotiate and execute an agreement with the lowest
  responsive bidder for a not-to-exceed sum of $1 50,000.

10.  Cabrillo Mole Revitalization Proiect Phase 2 Progressive Design Build Stage 1 Contract
  Award for Design and Engineering Services
  After hearing presentations from all three design-build teams and receiving feedback from
  the City Council, City Staff recommends the City Council award the contract for the
  Cabrillo Mole Revitalization, Phase 2 Progressive Design Build Stage 1 Project to
  Anderson Burton Construction, Inc. The Stage 1 contract is for the design and
  engineering elements of the project only. The City will negotiation with Anderson Burton
  Construction, Inc. to determine necessary consultants and refine the engineering and
  design scope.
  Recommended Action
  1. Award the contract for the Cabrillo Mole Revitalization, Phase 2 Progressive Design
  Build Stage 1 Project to Anderson Burton Construction, Inc. 2. Authorize the City Manager
  to negotiate and bring back a contract agreement for City Council approval.

6.  Repair and Maintenance of City Shoreboat Float

GENERAL BUSINESS

7.  Catalina Xtreme Parasail DBA Catalina Coastal Tours Transportation Permit
  Application
  1. City Council heard the presentation. 2. City Council discussed. 3. Consensus
  was met, approved the Transportation Permit for Catalina Xtreme Parasail DBA
  Catalina Coastal Tours to utilize a Residential Autoette vehicle permit to conduct
  City tours with stated conditions.
  Motion to approve made by Michael Ponce, seconded by Yesenia De La Rosa.
  (All Ayes)

8.  Pedicab Catalina Transportation Permit Application
  1. City Council heard the presentation. 2. City Council discussed. 3. Consensus
  was met, City Council approved a Transportation Permit for Joe Sampson’s
  Pedicab Catalina for one pedicab to conduct tours with stated conditions. 4. The
  approval allows for the operation of the pedicab on Front Street between Metropole
  and Sumner for a two-month period. The matter will be brought back to the Council
  for review. City staff will install appropriate signage indicating that pedicab access
  only is permitted on Front Street.
  Motion to approve made by Michael Ponce, seconded by Lisa Lavelle. (All Ayes)

9.  Consideration of Short-Term and Long-Term Rental Policy
  Consensus was met to continue talks about options to incentivize long-term
  rentals within the City and evaluate City long-term and short-term rental policies.
  City staff will return at a later date with additional information regarding the number
  of long-term rentals, potential grant funding opportunities (including CDBG funds),
  availability of private funding, and the possibility of placing a tax measure on the
  November ballot.

SUBJECT:  Fiscal Year 2025-2026 Third Quarter Treasurer’s Report

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Adopt the resolution accepting the FY25-26 Third Quarter
Treasurer’s Report.

REPORT SUMMARY: State and Municipal Codes require the Treasurer to submit within
30 days following each fiscal quarter a report summarizing the City’s cash and investment
balances. Attached is the Third Quarter Treasurer’s Report for FY25-26. The report was
shared with the City Treasurer prior to presentation to City Council.

The purpose of the report is to inform, on a quarterly basis, the City’s cash and investment
balances, the investment types, yields, and market values, and to ensure that the City’s
investments are in compliance with the City’s adopted investment policy. The report shows that
all of the City’s funds are in compliance with its investment policy. In general, operating cash is
held in US Bank checking accounts and any excess cash is invested in California’s Local
Agency Investment Fund (LAIF) and various certificates of deposit (CDs). In accordance with
Government Code sections 16429.1 and 53601 et seq., the City cannot invest more than 30%
of its portfolio in CDs. CDs accounted for 18.4% of the unrestricted cash and investments for
the quarter ended March 31, 2026.

The City did not have any CDs maturing during the quarter ended March 31, 2026. The City
takes a ladder approach with staggered maturities for its CD investments to balance its goals
of high rates in the short-term with stability to withstand market fluctuations in the longer-term.
The City will continue to assess for opportunities to increase its investment returns while
maintaining necessary liquidity and compliance with its investment policy.

The unrestricted cash balance for the third quarter of 2025-2026 totaled $22.71 million, a
decrease of $1.2 million from the third quarter of 2024-2025. The decrease in unrestricted cash
balance is largely attributable to increased capital outlays during the current fiscal year. The
unrestricted cash balance includes cash from enterprise funds (e.g. Harbor, Sewer, Saltwater,
and Solid Waste) not available for general government functions. While the majority of grant
funding is performed on a cash reimbursement basis, the unrestricted cash and investments
balance also includes $2 million in grant pre-funding received in preparation for construction of
the second phase of the Cabrillo Mole Ferry Improvement project that has not been spent as of
December 31, 2025. The City expended approximately $150,000 from this grant during the
third quarter of the current fiscal year. The City expects significant capital outlays on several
 major capital projects, including the second phase of the Cabrillo Mole Ferry Terminal
rehabilitation and the Five Corners Pedestrian Improvement project, which will reduce the
unrestricted cash balances over the next several quarters.

SUBJECT:  Waterside Project Change Conditions of Use-.- Catalina Snorkel and

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): City Council make the affirmative finding that conditions set
forth in the Avalon Municipal Code have been met and grant the amendment to the current
Waterside Permit to Catalina Snorkel and Scuba and add additional services, with the
following:

  1. Catalina Snorkel and Scuba will add the service of unwrapping fouled propellers and
  general light salvage and retrieval of items lost overboard within the Harbor.
  2. All personnel conducting dive services will have the appropriate dive certifications and
  training.
  3. When conducting any dive operations Catalina Snorkel and Scuba will notify and obtain
  permission from the Harbor Department prior to the dive.
  4. When diving in the Harbor, Catalina Scuba and Snorkel personnel will display a highly
  visible dive flag and take all precautions to avoid any boat traffic.
  5. if a skiff or boat is to be used in providing these services, all required and current
  registration/documentation will be provided to the Harbor Department.

REPORT SUMMARY: The applicant has submitted a Waterside Project Application to amend
conditions of use of their current waterside permit. Currently, the waterside permit authorizes
snorkeling/dive tours and instruction emanating from Lover’s Cove and Casino Point. Applicant
is requesting to add the services of unfouling propellers and light salvage within City waters.

While this proposal will add boat traffic to Harbor, it will not result in any substantial negative
impact upon Avalon Harbor floats, except as noted in subsection (2), below. The
recommendation is to approve the change in conditions of use provided all stipulations are
met.

Section 10-2.416 of the Municipal Code provides that a waterside permit may only be granted
where the City Council is able to make the following affirmative findings:
  (1)  The project will not result in a substantial alteration of the City’s present or
planned waterside uses of the Avalon Harbor
  (2)  With regard to transportation and circulation, the project (I) will not generate
substantial additional boat trips, including shoreboat trips, or other movement within A va/on
Harbor; (ii) will not have a substantial negative impact upon existing mooring, docking, or
 other anchorage facilities; (iii) will not have a substantial impact on other modes and systems
of transportation; (iv) will not result in substantial alterations of present patterns of circulation or
movement of people and /or goods; (v) will not increase traffic hazards to swimmers, boaters,
or other existing activities; and (vi) will not restrict or alter existing coastal access;

Impact: The Pleasure Pier floats see heavy usage in the summer months by rental kayaks,
pedal boats, small rental motor boats along with personal dinghies and pleasure boat traffic.

Mitigation: Catalina Snorkel and Scuba’s use of City floats is on-call only and they will be
required to contact the Harbor Office for docking arrangements upon arrival.

  (3)  The project will not have a substantial impact upon, and will not result in, a need
 for new or altered governmental services, including but not limited to fire, police, maintenance
of facilities, and harbor department services;
  (4)  The project will not result in the use of substantial amounts of fuel or other forms
of energy or substantially increase the demand upon existing energy or require the
development of new sources of energy;
  (5)  The project will not result in the need for new utility systems or a substantial
alteration of existing sources or systems for power, natural gas, communications, water,
sewage disposal or solid waste;
  (6)  The project will not obstruct any scenic vista or view open to the public, and will
not  result  in the creation of an aesthetically offensive site which is open to pub/ic view;
  (7)  The project will not result in a substantial negative impact upon the quality and
quantity of existing recreational opportunities or result in alterations or restrictions to coastal
access;
  (8)  The applicant is fit to be entrusted with the privileges of a permit, in that he has
not engaged in prior violations of the City’s harbor regulations, including the provisions of this
article, has timely paid any harbor-related fees and has not presented checks returned for
insufficient funds.

The Municipal Code also provides that the “City Council may deny the permit where the
impacts listed in paragraphs (1) through (8) above are cumulatively significant, even though
the individual impacts are limited. The City Council may approve a project where mitigation
measures eliminating significant impacts are incorporated into the project, and the approval
shall be conditioned upon the implementation of such mitigation measures. The failure to
comply and maintain any mitigation measures shall be a basis for suspension or revocation of
a waterside permit.”

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Increase service options for boaters, visitors and residents in the Avalon
Harbor area.

FISCAL IMPACTS: Unknown, potential increase in Harbor Use fees.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: Boaters, visitors and
residents will need to contact other businesses for these services.

SUBJECT:  Professional Services Agreement for On-Call Planning Consultant

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S):  1. Authorize an amendment to the current fiscal year
professional services agreement with Sagecrest Planning and Environmental, LLC for a not-to-
exceed sum of $225,000. 2. Authorize the City Manager or designee to execute a budget
adjustment transferring $50,000 from the General Planning/LCP Update Account Fund (10255-
6781) to the Planning Professional Services Account (10255-5005). 3. Authorize a budget
amendment in the amount of $25,000 to the Planning Professional Services Account (10255-
5005). 4. Authorize the City Manager to negotiate and execute a professional services
agreement with Sagecrest Planning and Environmental, LLC for on-call planning consultant
services for a two-year term for an annual cumulative total not to exceed amount of $200,000.00
commencing in FY 26-27.

REPORT SUMMARY: On February 20, 2024, City Council authorized the City Manager to
execute a professional services agreement with Sagecrest Planning and Environmental, LLC
(“Sagecrest”) for on-call planning consultant services for a not-to-exceed contract sum of
$150,000 for a one-year term with two optional one-year renewal terms.

Prior to engaging Sagerest, the City of Avalon had been seeking technical planning and
environmental review expertise. Staff determined that the need for a wide breadth of professional
planning expertise could best be delivered through a professional services contract. Sagecrest
has provided the day-to-day planning expertise in addition to being tasked with completing a
number of backlogged planning tasks.

In FY 25-26 the City engaged in a number of unique planning matters that required additional
services from Sagecrest including, but not limited to, review and consultation on the grant
application for the South Beach Restoration Project, regularly scheduled review and consultation
with city staff and CIH related to the new hospital, review and consultation associated with the
Civic Center Housing Project, plan review and consultation with Catalina Island Company related
to proposed employee housing project, plan review associated with two new hotel projects.
Additionally, the existing moratorium on short-term rentals ended and Sagecrest was
instrumental in instituting new STR regulations including a cap on the number of permitted units.
Termination of the moratorium opened up the pending STR applications for review and
presentation to Planning Commission at the end of 2025 through the first quarter of 2026. This
influx of activity, coupled with the aforementioned development projects, has generated
significant increased activity in the Planning Department not seen in recent years. As a result,
of the need for these increased services, an amendment to the Planning Professional Services
account of $75,000 is hereby requested.
 The agreement with Sagecrest has been extremely beneficial in allowing the City to utilize a
broad range of consultants with expertise in varying areas of planning, development and land
use entitlements. It is imperative that the city maintain and expand the current range of planning
expertise with the ongoing development projects that include the Civic Center Housing Project,
Island Company Housing Project, new Hospital construction, and the Cabrilto Mole Project.
Going forward, although many major projects are still pending, the reduction of STR applications
and reviews should reduce the overall services anticipated in FY 26-27 and it is proposed that
the Planning Professional Services be limited to $200,000.

Staff continues to evaluate the cost for services provided by Sagecrest compared to the potential
cost of a fully weighted full-time Planning Director salary ($180,000) and benefits ($63,000).
Even with the proposed increase, the City still recognizes a cost savings and access to far
greater breadth of expertise than a full-time Planning Director model. Additionally, due to
Sagecrest’s experience in the field, the City has experienced a continued cost savings in
planning related legal fees. The increase in planning-related activity during the current fiscal year
has been partially offset by increases in planning-related revenues, with $77,101 collected
through March 2026 compared to $35,041 collected during the prior fiscal year.

Historically, the city has budgeted an additional $50,000 for General Planning and LCP updates
(Account 10255-6781). Due to Sagecrest taking on these obligations, the city has not spent any
of those funds in the current fiscal year. As a result, staff proposes to offset a portion of the
increased fees with a budget adjustment of $50,000 from 10255-6781 to the Planning
Professional Services account (10255-5005). The balance of the proposed increase is requested
in the form of a budget amendment of $25,000 to account 10255-5005.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Sustainability of operations.

FISCAL IMPACTS: FY 2025-26 Planning Services budget (account number 10255-5055) will
be increased by $75,000 to $225,000 and the future annual budget will be set at $200,000.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The City will not have
specialized planning support.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Implement City Council direction.

agenda pursuant to the Brown Act.

SUBJECT:  ENGEO On-Call Engineering Services Contract

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): 1. Make the affirmative finding that the City will not gain a
competitive advantage by bidding and can contract work more economically or efficiently
pursuant to Avalon Municipal Code Section 3-4.111 (C), and 2. Award a professional services
contract for on-call engineering, materials testing and inspection for an amount not-to-exceed
an annual cumulative total for all services of $100,000 to ENGEO, Inc. for a three-year term.

REPORT SUMMARY: The City has contracted with ESG Engineering, Inc. (ESG) to provide
on-call engineering services since 2015. A sub-consultant of ESG, ENGEO, Inc. has been
used to provide geotechnical engineering resources including development of the geotechnical
investigation of the Cabrillo Mole Multimodal Transportation Hub in September 2021,
Geotechnical Exploration reports for 206 E. VVhittley Ave., South Beach Seawall and Beach
Restoration Plans, the Green Pleasure Pier and Club Dock Pile Installation Projects and many
others City Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) Projects.

The City is currently engaged in preconstruction and construction phases of a number of highly
complex CIP projects that require geotechnical engineering services as well as materials
testing and inspections. The City anticipates a high level of budgeted expenditures in the
forthcoming fiscal years for these services.

As ENGEO is currently engaged with City Staff on these projects, City Staff recommends the
City Council make the affirmative finding that the City will not gain a competitive advantage by
bidding and can contract work more economically or efficiently pursuant to Avalon Municipal
Code (AMC) Section 3-4.111 (C), and award a professional services contract for on-call
engineering, materials testing and inspection for an amount not-to-exceed an annual
cumulative total for all services of $100,000 to ENGEO, Inc. for a three-year term.

Due to the level of nuance and the timing of these projects and ENEGO’s current engagement
and understanding of the logistics of performing work on Catalina Island, City Staff believe
there will be no competitive advantage to bidding the on-call engineering services, materials
testing and inspection contract at this time. AMC Section 3-4.111 (c) outlines an exception
from bidding and other competitive procedures for economic efficiency. Per the AMC:

  If a competitive market does not exist, or the City will not gain a competitive advantage
  by using the formal contract bid or other competitive procedure, or where the public
   project, goods or se,vices may be obtained more economically or efficiently without the
  procedure, the City may dispense with formal bidding or other competitive procedures.

Additionally, City Staff anticipate a cost savings by contracting directly with ENGEO and
avoiding overhead/”mark-up” costs working through ESG.

Task orders for on-call services will be driven by the approved budget. Annually funds cannot
be spent unless they are a part of an approved, budgeted, project or account, or receive
additional City Council approval in accordance with the approved budget and fiscal policies.

FISCAL IMPACTS: Not-to-exceed $100,000 for all task orders per 12-month period for all
approved on-call engineer services, for a contract of three years. Expenditures will be
allocated to the appropriate budgeted project.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Fiscal responsibility.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The City will need to
procure the engineering related services for each project and task order which may take more
time and cost additional funds or procure services through the existing ESG contract with a
contract mark-up.

SUBJECT:  Cabrillo Mole Geotechnical Study Drilling RFP and Contract Award

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): 1. Authorize City Staff to develop and solicit a request for
proposals for qualified firms to conduct drilling services to accommodate a geotechnical study
to support the Cabrillo Mole Revitalization Project. 2. Pursuant to Avalon Municipal Code
Section 3-4.205, authorize the City Manager to negotiate and execute an agreement with the
lowest responsive bidder for a not-to-exceed sum of $150,000.

REPORT SUMMARY: ENGEO, Inc. performed a geotechnical investigation of the Cabrillo
Mole Multimodal Transportation Hub in September 2021. In order to begin the Cabrillo Mole
Revitalization Project, the City must provide the selected Cabrillo Mole Revitalization Project
contractor an updated geotechnical study that reflects current building code standards as well
as the current geotechnical conditions of the substructure of the Cabrillo Mole.

In order for any geotechnical engineer to perform an analysis, exploration pits must be drilled
from the Cabrillo Mole’s surface.

City Staff estimate drilling services to cost approximately $150,000. Avalon Municipal Code
Section 3-4.205 requires public projects between $60,001 and $200,000 to be contracted by
informal bid procedure. To mitigate the impact during the visitor season, time is of the essence.
City Staff plan to develop and solicit a request for proposals from qualified firms for 15 days
as required by the AMC.

City Staff request authorization for the City Manager to award a contract to the lowest
responsive bidder for a not-to-exceed sum of $150,000. If the City does not receive any bids
responsive to the request, or if the lowest responsive bid is greater than $150,000, City Staff
will return to City Council for further direction. It is the City’s goal to complete all drilling
services prior to the start of Memorial Day weekend May 22, 2026. By granting authority to
  —

the City Manager to execute an agreement to the lowest responsive bidder, the City be able to
expedite completion of the work while meeting all procurement requirements.

FISCAL IMPACTS: This project is budgeted in the FY 25-26 CIP Budget  —  Project # 180003-1
and will utilize general funding resources.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Infrastructure repairs.
 CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The work will not be
completed.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Draft and solicit an RFP, then execute contract agreement with the
lowest responsive bidder.

SUBJECT:  Cabrillo Mole Revitalization Project Phase 2 Progressive Design
  Build Stage 1 Contract Award for Design and Engineering Services

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): 1. Award the contract for the Cabrillo Mole Revitalization,
Phase 2 Progressive Design Build Stage 1 Project to Anderson Burton Construction, Inc. 2.
Authorize the City Manager to negotiate and bring back a contract agreement for City Council
approval.

REPORT SUMMARY: On November 17, 2025, the City of Avalon published a request for
qualifications (RFQ) for the Progressive Design-Build Cabrillo Mole Revitalization Phase II
Project.

The City conducted a mandatory pre-bid conference in person and virtually on December 11,
2025. The meeting included an overview of the requirements set forth in the RFQ, a walk
through the City’s design intent, as well as a visit to the Cabrillo Mole to examine existing
conditions and operational expectations. The original bid deadline was extended from January
22 to February 5, 2026 to allow potential respondents more time to provide comprehensive
responses to the RFQ.

The City received three proposals from qualified design-build teams by the stated deadline  —

A.J. Padelford & Sons, Inc., Anderson Burton Construction, Inc., and Benchmark Contractors,
Inc. City Staff have conducted a thorough analysis of the proposals received, and conducted
two meetings/interviews with each design-build teams.

City Staff arranged for the City Council to hear presentations with each team at two Special
City Council Meetings held on March 24 and 31, 2026. The design-build teams were requested
to provide a 30-minute presentation that would include an introduction of their team and an
overview of their understanding of the project and their intended approach.

After hearing presentations from all three design-build teams and receiving feedback from the
City Council, City Staff recommends the City Council award the contract for the Cabrillo Mole
Revitalization, Phase 2 Progressive Design Build Stage 1 Project to Anderson Burton
Construction, Inc.

While City Staff made the determination that all three firms that provided SOQs were qualified
and capable of completing the Cabrillo Mole Revitalization Project, Anderson Burton
Construction, Inc., was identified to be the best partner for the City. Anderson Burton
 Construction, Inc., partnered with RRM Design Group, has an extensive resume of successful
partnerships featuring Spanish Heritage style public projects  an aesthetic identified as
  —

preferred by the community at large as well as, the City Council and business stakeholders.
RRM Design Group also has experience specific to projects on Catalina Island. While cost is
not the sole factor in this recommendation, it is a very important element of the project.
Anderson Burton Construction, Inc.’s project budget for Stage 1 and Stage 2 very closely
aligned with the City’s expectation of services.

City Staff request authorization for the City Manager to negotiate and bring back a contract
agreement for Stage I of this project. The Stage 1 contract is for the design and engineering
elements of the project only. The City will negotiation with Anderson Burton Construction, Inc.
to determine necessary consultants and refine the engineering and design scope. If the City
and Anderson Burton Construction, Inc. cannot successfully negotiate a contract agreement,
City Staff will return to City Council to request authorization to negotiate a contract with
Benchmark Contractors, Inc. or A.J. Padelford & Sons Construction, Inc.

City Staff anticipate successfully executing a contract by early May. City Staff will return to City
Council for regular updates on the design process as well as for final approval of the
architectural design. After the design is approved, City Staff may request authorization to
negotiate and award a contract with Anderson Burton Construction, Inc. for the Stage 2  —

construction  —  contract or may request to go to solicit a request for bids using the final
construction plans.

FISCAL IMPACTS: This project is budgeted in the FY 25-26 CIP Budget  —  Project # 180003-i
and will utilize a combination of grant and general funding resources.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Infrastructure updates.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The City will not have
direction on how to proceed with the Cabrillo Mole Revitalization Project.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Begin negotiations with Anderson Burton Construction, Inc. and bring
back a contract for City Council consideration.
